A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Nirvana and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, reasoning, retrieval, and MRI reconstruction experiments, including ablations and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds specialized-domain perplexity results, inference-speed measurements, and analyses of fast-parameter dynamics.

M1.justification: The Trigger/Updater architecture, weight-bank parameterization, CL-OGD objective, conditional interpolation, and two-stage frozen-backbone MRI procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 and the configuration tables clarify existing components rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: v2 Section 4.2.1 adds training and evaluation on MIMIC-III clinical notes, April–October 2024 financial news associated with FinGPT, and Asylex refugee-status documents. This substantially extends specialized-domain coverage beyond v1's MRI application. Existing general-language and MRI coverage remains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including the relocated E2E-VarNet and UDNO comparisons. New domain and throughput experiments reuse existing comparator architectures. RAG and Miras receive conceptual comparisons, without reported experimental evaluation.

E3.justification: New protocols include three-epoch domain fine-tuning, throughput evaluation with 4096-token prompts and batch size 4, and dynamics measurements over 1,024 sequences using greedy decoding and layer/token buckets. The reported reference learning rate also changes from 0.01 in v1 Section 2.2 to 0.001 in v2 Table 10; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 4.3 and Tables 7–8 examine how Trigger update magnitudes, directions, and learning rates vary with depth and token position. Domain-text and throughput experiments extend the noTrigger ablation. Existing RoPE, length-extrapolation, MRI undersampling, and toy-example analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 7–8 introduce descriptive distribution reporting through means, 95th percentiles, and large-update fractions over 1,024 sequences. Existing MRI uncertainty values are unchanged. No new repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds throughput results, including 516 tokens/s for Nirvana versus 568 without Trigger, and specialized-domain perplexities of 8.25, 7.88, and 7.22, averaging 7.78 versus 9.30 without Trigger. Tables 7–8 add parameter-dynamics findings. Original experimental tables retain their numerical values, and existing plotted results are reused.

T1.justification: v2 Equations 10–12 introduce mathematical definitions for layer-wise relative update magnitude, cosine change, and token-wise update speed. These are limited additions supporting the new diagnostics. Existing method equations remain substantively unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central architectural contribution and general-to-specialist claim remain. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add an explicit lowest-perplexity claim across biomedicine, finance, and law, while emphasizing Trigger's benefits across evaluation tasks. These extend the empirical claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly limits conclusions about scaling, architectural tuning, and clinical validity, identifying synthetic MRI undersampling and automatically generated reports as constraints. Section 4.3 adds interpretations of early task alignment followed by more conservative adaptation. Appendix C also explains complementarity with external retrieval.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies important architecture details, including 24 layers, four prelude layers, hidden size 2048, 64 weight-bank blocks, and Trigger QKV dimension 512. Algorithm 1 supplies explicit CL-OGD operation ordering and parallelization information. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation beyond v1's basic training and MRI settings.

R1.justification: New Appendices C–D and Tables 14–15 substantially develop positioning against RAG and Miras, including distinctions in memory, parameterization, and adaptation, plus a stated reason for omitting a controlled Miras experiment. Specialized-corpus references are added, several architecture references are removed, and the existing hybrid/TTT review is condensed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory framing, MRI discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work moves from the appendix into the main text, existing MRI comparisons are redistributed, and the appendix structure is extensively reorganized. Terminology distinguishing fast hyper-parameters, fast weights, and the weight bank becomes more explicit.

P2.justification: The branded single-column report becomes a two-column paper, with extensive resizing and relocation of existing displays. New tables present notation, configurations, throughput, domain results, dynamics, and conceptual comparisons, alongside Algorithm 1. Existing scientific figures are reused rather than replaced with new findings.

improvement.justification: The added domain and throughput experiments give more direct support to specialization and efficiency claims, while fuller implementation details and explicit clinical limitations improve transparency. These gains are tempered by a new internal inconsistency: Table 10's reference rate of 0.001 and sigmoid gate conflict with Table 7's adaptive-rate mean of 0.00178 and 95th percentile of 0.00342. This weakens confidence in the new dynamics analysis and limits the overall improvement.
